matches.why: Same defect: readBytes at ValueReader.java:88 allocates new byte[(int)contentLength] from a peer-chosen 4-byte length before readFully, with only the `contentLength < Integer.MAX_VALUE` cast guard. Both name line 86-89, both identify the guard as cast-safety rather than a limit, and both reproduce OutOfMemoryError under -Xmx64m from four wire bytes.

Same defect: unbounded mutual recursion readFieldValue <-> readTable/readArray with no depth parameter on any of the three one-argument signatures (lines 158/139/237), reachable inside one default AMQP frame and surfacing as StackOverflowError. Cited lines differ (158 vs 183) only because each picks a different point on the same cycle; the exploit mechanism and the measured wire cost per level are the same.

Same defect: lines 91-94 of readBytes throw UnsupportedOperationException (a RuntimeException) for declared lengths at or above Integer.MAX_VALUE, escaping the `throws IOException` / MalformedFrameException error channel every other rejection in the class uses (line 217). Identical location, identical trigger, identical wrong-exception-type mechanism.

Same defect: the generate-sources binding runs codegen.py against ${codegen.dir} (default ${basedir}/deps/rabbitmq_codegen) with no revision, hash or signature pinning the external tree, and build-helper adds the generated sources to the published jar; both also flag the in-umbrella profile auto-activating on ../../UMBRELLA.md and silently redirecting deps.dir. Line numbers 613 vs 595 are two points inside the same plugin execution block.

Same defect: dependency risk is unmeasured because no advisory source was consulted offline, and the pins sit on possibly end-of-support branches where scanner silence is not a clean result. Both name the same branches (logback 1.2, Jetty 9.4, groovy-all 2.4.21 on the build path, slf4j 1.7 shipped) and both explicitly rule out floating ranges as the finding.

Same defect: line 151-152 `if(!table.containsKey(name)) table.put(name, value)` resolves duplicate field-table names first-wins and discards the later occurrence with no error or record, producing a parser differential against readers that resolve last-wins. Same line, same mechanism, same differential framing.

hardest_call: L08 vs R04 vs R05. R04's evidence ends by noting the pom wires no dependency-vulnerability gate and that grep for cyclonedx/spdx/sbom/dependency-check/enforcer returns nothing - which is exactly R05's subject - so R05 could look like a second half of the same dependency story. I kept them apart and matched L08 to R04 because the mechanisms differ: L08 and R04 are both about specific pinned branches whose support status makes advisory silence unmeasured (a remediation-is-migration problem on named components), while R05 is about the build emitting no bill of materials and no gate at all (a producer-side provenance problem that exists regardless of how old any branch is). R04 mentions the gate only in passing while describing the unmeasured-dependency finding, which is precisely the kind of passing mention the rule says not to match on. Second-hardest: L09 (no maximum enforced on the table/array declared lengths at lines 142/240) against R07 - L09's write-up references F-001/readBytes, but its own location and evidence are the two other lengths and it explicitly claims no impact of its own, so it is a distinct hardening defect with no counterpart on the right.
